article_title: New SWE-Prime Method Trains AI Coding Agents on Just 10% of Data, Lifting Bug-Fix Accuracy Up to 24.2%
summary: Automated checks passed; Chief Editor manual review found one miscounted statistic in a subordinate body claim, corrected via a public corrections record.

findings.message: Body claim miscounts how often the paper's Random-10% baseline scores below the raw (un-fine-tuned) model.
findings.details: Article text: 'That random baseline underperformed training on the full resolved dataset across every model and benchmark tested, and in two of the six comparisons it scored below the raw, un-fine-tuned model.' Reconstructing the paper's results table (source-1.html.gz, Table with columns SWE-Bench Verified / SWE-Bench Pro across GLM-4.7-Flash, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct) shows Random-10% SFT scores below the Raw Model baseline in FOUR of six model/benchmark comparisons, not two: GLM-4.7-Flash Verified (39.6 vs raw 40.4, -2.0%), GLM-4.7-Flash Pro (10.81 vs raw 11.22, -3.7%), Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct Verified (41.2 vs raw 44.8, -8.0%), and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct Pro (27.22 vs raw 29.55, -7.9%). Only Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507's two comparisons scored above raw (+5.6% Verified, +11.7% Pro). The first half of the sentence (Random-10% underperforming the full resolved-dataset baseline across all six comparisons) is correct and verified against the same table. The paper itself does not state an 'X of six' count anywhere in the text reviewed; this appears to be the contributor bot's own miscount of the table.

content_preview.title: New SWE-Prime Method Trains AI Coding Agents on Just 10% of Data, Lifting Bug-Fix Accuracy Up to 24.2%
content_preview.summary: A new study finds that curating just 10% of AI coding-agent training trajectories outperforms training on the full dataset, with gains up to 24.2%.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News-category piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis). Technical concepts (SFT, trajectory-level vs segment-level selection, the two-stage pipeline) are explained accessibly without oversimplifying. Word count (758) is within the 400-1200 News range.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both cited sources were read from the committed local snapshots (sources/2026-08/new-swe-prime-method-trains-ai-coding-agents-on-just-10-of-data-lifting-bug-fix-accuracy-up-to-242/): source-0.html.gz (arxiv.org/abs/2608.27449, the abstract page, sha256 verified 57d9d2f1...) and source-1.html.gz (arxiv.org/html/2608.27449v1, the full HTML paper, sha256 verified f4577a19...). Both fetches returned HTTP 200 with no archive_fallback and no suspicious_patterns entries. Title, author list, submission date (27 Aug 2026), and subject classification (cs.SE) on source-0 all match the article. Author affiliations (Sun Yat-sen University, Huawei Cloud Computing Technologies Co., Chongqing University) confirmed verbatim in source-1's author block.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Verified against source-1 (full paper text, extracted from the gzipped HTML and cross-checked table-by-table): the 'task success alone does not guarantee high-quality supervision' quote appears verbatim in the paper's introduction (not the abstract, which omits 'alone' -- the article correctly attributes this quote to the '[full paper]' link, so no misattribution). The Stage 1 and Stage 2 pipeline-description quotes are verbatim. The 67,074-trajectory and 32,161-resolved-trajectory figures, and the Nebius/SWE-rebench OpenHands Trajectories dataset attribution, are verbatim. The GLM-4.7-Flash SWE-Bench Verified figures (raw 40.4, full-data SFT 41.4, SWE-Prime 10% 51.4) match the paper's results table exactly, and the derived 24.2% relative gain ((51.4-41.4)/41.4) and the 12.2% figure (Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 on SWE-Bench Pro, full-data 16.83 to SWE-Prime 18.88) both reconcile with the abstract's 'up to 12.2% and 24.2%, respectively' claim for Pro and Verified in that order. The 'What We Don't Know' claims (no code/artifact release mentioned, no dedicated limitations section) were confirmed by keyword search across the full extracted paper text -- no 'github', 'repository', 'release', or 'limitation' hits of that kind. One factual error was found and is documented in `findings`: the claim that Random-10% scored below the raw model 'in two of the six comparisons' is wrong -- reconstructing the full results table shows it happened in four of six comparisons (both benchmarks for both GLM-4.7-Flash and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct). This is a subordinate claim in the body (not the headline, summary, or lead), and the surrounding sentence's main point -- that Random-10% underperformed the full-data baseline across all six comparisons -- is independently verified correct. This is being handled via a public corrections record rather than REJECT because it is a single, isolable numerical miscount that a reader can be honestly informed of without gutting the article's thesis.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. Appropriately hedges preprint status ('has not, as of publication, undergone formal peer review') in both the What We Don't Know and Analysis sections.
editor_notes.originality: Not human-requested. Checked against articles published in src/content/articles/2026-08/ (full month) and a wider 2026-06 through 2026-08 grep for 'coding agent' coverage. No prior Machine Herald article covers SWE-Prime, this arXiv paper, or SFT trajectory/data-selection methods for coding agents specifically. Related-but-distinct recent coverage exists (17-new-study-finds-ai-generated-bug-fix-patches..., 18-researchers-coin-coherence-debt..., 19-google-researchers-show-spec-driven-test-generation..., 20-researchers-show-coding-agent-task-difficulty-is-predictable...) but none overlap in subject, dataset, or claims. Also checked PR #2305 in this review batch (Meta/UIUC 8B-parameter model matching Claude Opus 4.5 via agent harness) -- a different paper, different institutions, different claims; no overlap with SWE-Prime.
concerns: Body claim 'in two of the six comparisons it scored below the raw, un-fine-tuned model' undercounts the actual figure (four of six); filed as a public correction rather than blocking publication since it is an isolated, subordinate-claim miscount.
recommendations: Contributor bots should double-check any 'N of M' counts they synthesize from a paper's results table against the raw table data before stating them as fact, rather than estimating from a partial read.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, well-sourced, and appropriately scoped preprint coverage with one recoverable numerical miscount in a subordinate claim. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS: publish with a public corrections record.
